simple: a read, change and write of one memory word that no other thread can cut into.
analogy: pressing the tally counter's button.
precise: a read-modify-write on a 32-, 64- (or for some operations 16- or 128-) bit word in global or shared memory, guaranteed to be performed without interference from other threads in its scope; CUDA exposes it as atomicAdd, atomicSub, atomicExch, atomicMin, atomicMax, atomicInc, atomicDec, atomicCAS, atomicAnd, atomicOr, atomicXor.
source: D1 of F6-13 (NVIDIA, "CUDA C++ Programming Guide") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: which threads the "cannot be cut into" promise covers.
analogy: a counter for one table, one for the hall, one for the whole restaurant chain.
precise: atomicAdd_block is atomic with respect to the threads of the block, atomicAdd of the device, atomicAdd_system also of the host and other devices; available from compute capability 6.0.
source: D1 of F6-13 (NVIDIA, "CUDA C++ Programming Guide") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: one of the equal slices of shared memory that can each serve one word at a time.
analogy: one drawer of the table.
precise: shared memory is divided into banks that can be accessed simultaneously; successive 32-bit words are assigned to successive banks. Not a DRAM bank (HW203).
source: D1 of F6-11 (NVIDIA, "CUDA C++ Programming Guide") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: several threads of one warp want different words from the same bank, so they are served one after another.
analogy: two helpers reaching into the same drawer for different things.
precise: the access is split into as many conflict-free passes as the largest number of distinct words requested from one bank (the conflict degree).
source: D1 of F6-11 (NVIDIA, "CUDA C++ Programming Guide") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a "wait here until everyone in the block arrives" point.
analogy: nobody starts reading the table until every bowl is on it.
precise: a block-wide barrier: no thread of the block continues past it until all threads of the block have reached it, and shared-memory writes made before it are visible to the block after it. Full treatment in F6-12.
source: D1 of F6-10 (NVIDIA, "CUDA C++ Programming Guide") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: one category of a histogram and its counter.
analogy: the counter for "plums".
precise: one element h[k]; in CUB's HistogramEven, bins are equal-width ranges between a lower and an upper level, and "the number of histogram bins is (num_levels - 1)" (quoted from the installed header).
source: H2 of F6-17 (CUB 2.0.1 headers as installed (libcub-dev 2.0.1-2), read in this build: cub/device/device_histogram.cuh (number of bins), cub/agent/agent_histogram.cuh (privatized shared-memory or global-memory bins). Tier 1.) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a reduction tree up, then a tree down that hands each subtree its starting value.
analogy: collect counts up to the head of the hall, then hand starting numbers back down.
precise: up-sweep and down-sweep, 2 log₂ n steps, about 2n additions (work-efficient); exclusive result.
source: D3 of F6-16 (Hwu, Kirk, El Hajj, "Programming Massively Parallel Processors: A Hands-on Approach") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: many threads read the very same word, and one read serves them all.
analogy: one helper lifts the spice out and everyone looks at it.
precise: threads that read the same 32-bit word do not conflict; the word is delivered to all of them.
source: D1 of F6-11 (NVIDIA, "CUDA C++ Programming Guide") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: lanes swap values with a partner whose number differs in one bit.
analogy: helpers swap with the helper opposite in their group of 2, 4, 8, …
precise: __shfl_xor_sync(m, v, k) pairs lane i with lane i XOR k; log₂ width steps give every lane the full reduction (all-reduce).
source: R1 of F6-15 (run of Listing 1 (university/labs/F6-15/warp_sim.log), g++ 13.3.0, exit code 0.) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: neighbouring threads storing to neighbouring addresses, so the stores combine into few memory transactions.
analogy: putting neighbouring jars on one shelf in one trip.
precise: the store counterpart of coalescing (F6-08); in the 32-byte-segment model of Listing 2, a warp storing 32 consecutive floats touches 4 segments, 32 floats one row apart touch 32.
source: R2 of F6-19 (run of Listing 2 (transpose_audit.log), g++ 13.3.0, exit code 0.) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: "write my new value only if the old value is still what I saw."
analogy: replacing the sticky note only if it still shows the number you read.
precise: atomicCAS(addr, compare, val) reads old, stores val if old == compare, and returns old; any atomic read-modify-write can be built from it with a retry loop.
source: D1 of F6-13 (NVIDIA, "CUDA C++ Programming Guide") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: many threads wanting the same address at the same time.
analogy: the queue in front of the one counter.
precise: atomics on one address are performed one after another, so their throughput falls as more of them target it; the cost per operation depends on the GPU.
source: D2 of F6-13 (NVIDIA, "CUDA C++ Best Practices Guide") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: many updates aimed at the same bin at the same time.
analogy: the queue at the apple counter when every crate is apples.
precise: atomic updates to one address are serialised (F6-13); its cost depends on the input's distribution, so a histogram's speed depends on its data.
source: D1 of F6-17 (NVIDIA, "CUDA C++ Programming Guide") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a special way to start a kernel that promises all its blocks run at once.
analogy: asking for the whole hall, and only being let in if every table fits.
precise: cudaLaunchCooperativeKernel; the device must report the cooperative-launch attribute, and the number of blocks may not exceed the occupancy calculator's blocks per SM times the number of SMs.
source: H1 of F6-12 (CUDA 12.0 headers as installed (nvidia-cuda-dev 12.0.146~12.0.1-4build4), read in this build: cuda_runtime_api.h (comment of cudaLaunchCooperativeKernel, quoted), sm_20_intrinsics.h (__syncthreads_count/and/or), sm_) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: how fast the GPU can just copy the matrix, the ceiling a transpose is measured against.
analogy: moving the jars without turning them.
precise: E5's target is "X % of your E2 copy bandwidth"; Listing 1's copyTile uses the same tiles and threads without transposing and reports each kernel's time as a percentage of it.
source: C1 of F6-19 (Systems Curriculum (this project), milestone E5 (goal, read, build and accept quoted). A map, not a source (AH-4).) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a one-pass device scan where each tile publishes its total and looks back at earlier tiles' published values.
analogy: the board by the door.
precise: Merrill and Garland's method: per-tile status words (not ready, aggregate available, inclusive prefix available); a tile sums predecessors' aggregates until it meets an inclusive prefix; about 2n memory accesses; implemented in CUB's DeviceScan.
source: S2 of F6-16 (Duane Merrill and Michael Garland, "Single-pass Parallel Prefix Scan with Decoupled Look-back") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a small group of bits of the key looked at in one pass.
analogy: one digit of the plate number.
precise: (key >> shift) & (2d − 1); with d = 4 a digit has 16 values, with d = 8, 256.
source: R2 of F6-18 (run of Listing 2 (lsd_sort.log), g++ 13.3.0, exit code 0.) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: each output is the total of the elements before it; the first is the identity.
analogy: "where my plates start".
precise: y0 = identity, yi = ⊕j < i xj; exclusive = inclusive shifted right by one.
source: D3 of F6-16 (Hwu, Kirk, El Hajj, "Programming Massively Parallel Processors: A Hands-on Approach") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: each thread handles element i, then i + (all threads of the grid), and so on.
analogy: each helper takes every N-th plate from the long counter.
precise: for (i = global id; i < n; i += gridDim.x * blockDim.x); decouples the grid size from n, so a fixed, occupancy-sized grid covers any input.
source: D2 of F6-14 (NVIDIA, "CUDA C++ Best Practices Guide") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a point that all threads of all blocks must reach before any continues.
analogy: a bell for the whole hall.
precise: safe only when every block of the grid is resident at the same time; CUDA provides it through cooperative groups (this_grid().sync()) for kernels started with a cooperative launch.
source: D1 of F6-12 (NVIDIA, "CUDA C++ Programming Guide") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the few extra values just outside a tile that the threads at its edges also need.
analogy: the extra bowls just past the ends of the group's stretch.
precise: the elements outside a block's output range that its computation reads; for a 1-D stencil of radius R, R elements on each side.
source: D3 of F6-10 (Wen-mei Hwu, David Kirk, Izzat El Hajj, "Programming Massively Parallel Processors: A Hands-on Approach") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: in step k, every element adds the element 2k places before it.
analogy: everybody looks 1, then 2, then 4 places back and adds.
precise: log₂ n steps, about n log₂ n additions; not work-efficient but short; needs two buffers or a barrier between read and write.
source: D3 of F6-16 (Hwu, Kirk, El Hajj, "Programming Massively Parallel Processors: A Hands-on Approach") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a count of how many items fall into each category.
analogy: the tally board by the door, one counter per kind of fruit.
precise: for input values xi and a bin function b(x) with B possible results, the array h[k] = |{ i : b(xi) = k }|, k = 0 … B − 1; the bins add up to the number of items.
source: D3 of F6-17 (Wen-mei Hwu, David Kirk, Izzat El Hajj, "Programming Massively Parallel Processors: A Hands-on Approach") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: each output includes its own element.
analogy: "plates up to and including mine".
precise: yi = ⊕j ≤ i xj; std::inclusive_scan.
source: D3 of F6-16 (Hwu, Kirk, El Hajj, "Programming Massively Parallel Processors: A Hands-on Approach") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: an index that does not fit in its integer type wraps around.
analogy: a plate numbering that goes from 2,147,483,647 back to a negative number.
precise: blockIdx.x * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x is computed in 32-bit unsigned arithmetic and wraps at 2^32; stored in an int, it is negative from 2^31 on.
source: R7 of F6-14 (PTX of sumBytes32 and sumBytes64, sm_80 (ptx_index.log), compiled only.) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: changing the bits of signed numbers or floats so that sorting them as unsigned numbers gives the right order.
analogy: relabelling plates so the shelf order is right.
precise: the installed CUB header lists them: unsigned keys "used directly"; signed: "the sign bit is inverted"; positive floats: "the sign bit is inverted"; negative floats: "the full key is inverted".
source: R6 of F6-18 (CUB header excerpt (cub_radix.log), read only.) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a thread's position in its warp, 0 to width − 1.
analogy: a helper's seat number in the row.
precise: threadIdx.x % warpSize for one-dimensional blocks.
source: D1 of F6-15 (NVIDIA, "CUDA C++ Programming Guide") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: an increment that disappears because another thread overwrote it.
analogy: two sticky notes that both say 42.
precise: the outcome of a data race on a read-modify-write; the final value is smaller than the number of increments, and different between runs.
source: R2 of F6-13 (run of Listing 2 (lost.log), g++ 13.3.0, exit code 0.) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: sort by the lowest digit first, the highest last.
analogy: last digit of the plate number first.
precise: after pass p, keys are sorted by their lowest p digits, provided every pass is stable; the last pass leaves them fully sorted.
source: D4 of F6-18 (Thomas H. Cormen, Charles E. Leiserson, Ronald L. Rivest, Clifford Stein, "Introduction to Algorithms") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: an instruction that orders a thread's own memory writes as others see them, without waiting for anybody.
analogy: putting the bowl down firmly before raising your hand, so whoever sees the hand also sees the bowl.
precise: orders the calling thread's memory accesses before and after it as observed by other threads (block, device or system scope for the three variants); unlike a barrier it waits for no other thread. Compare the C++ fences of F2-39.
source: D1 of F6-12 (NVIDIA, "CUDA C++ Programming Guide") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: adding a private copy into the global counters.
analogy: one helper per kind walks the table's count to the wall.
precise: after a barrier, threads of the block each take some bins and do atomicAdd(&global[b], local[b]), skipping zeros; at most B global atomics per block.
source: R1 of F6-17 (build and run of Listing 1 (university/labs/F6-17/histogram.log), CUDA 12.0; untested on hardware, exit code 1.) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: adding unused elements at the end of each row so that rows start in different banks.
analogy: sliding each card along by one drawer.
precise: choosing a pitch that is not a multiple of the bank count (for example 33 instead of 32) so that a column of the array spreads over all banks.
source: D2 of F6-11 (NVIDIA, "CUDA C++ Best Practices Guide") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: summing in a tree instead of a line, which keeps rounding errors small.
analogy: adding small piles to small piles, never a coin to a mountain.
precise: the error bound grows with log₂ n instead of n; a GPU tree reduction is a pairwise sum in a particular order. Compare Kahan's compensated sum (F0-75).
source: R4 of F6-14 (run of Listing 4 (sum_check.log), g++ 13.3.0, exit code 0.) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the list of lanes that promise to take part in a warp operation.
analogy: the helpers who agreed to pass hands this round.
precise: the first argument of every _sync warp function; each named lane must execute the same call (with the same mask) before any of them gets the result; __activemask() returns the lanes currently executing, which is not the same as the lanes that should take part.
source: D1 of F6-15 (NVIDIA, "CUDA C++ Programming Guide") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: how many elements one row of a 2-D array really takes in memory.
analogy: how many drawers one recipe card covers, including empty ones.
precise: the distance, in elements, between the starts of consecutive rows; for float t[32][33] the pitch is 33.
source: D3 of F6-11 (Wen-mei Hwu, David Kirk, Izzat El Hajj, "Programming Massively Parallel Processors: A Hands-on Approach") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: each group keeps its own private copy of the counters and adds it to the shared result once at the end.
analogy: a tally sheet on each table, carried to the wall when the table is done.
precise: replicate the output (here the B bins) per block (or per warp or thread), update the copies with low contention, then merge them into the global result; correct for any associative and commutative update.
source: D3 of F6-17 (Wen-mei Hwu, David Kirk, Izzat El Hajj, "Programming Massively Parallel Processors: A Hands-on Approach") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: two threads touch the same memory, at least one writes, and nothing fixes their order.
analogy: grabbing a neighbour's bowl without waiting for the bell.
precise: conflicting accesses not ordered by synchronization; the result depends on scheduling. The same idea as in SP203 (F2-35), now between GPU threads.
source: D1 of F6-12 (NVIDIA, "CUDA C++ Programming Guide") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: sorting by looking at one digit at a time instead of comparing whole keys.
analogy: putting plates in order by the last digit, then the middle, then the first.
precise: a non-comparison sort that treats a key as a sequence of d-bit digits and distributes keys by one digit per pass; for b-bit keys it needs ⌈b/d⌉ passes, each linear in n.
source: D3 of F6-18 (Wen-mei Hwu, David Kirk, Izzat El Hajj, "Programming Massively Parallel Processors: A Hands-on Approach") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: read a value, change it, write it back.
analogy: reading the counter, adding in your head, writing a sticky note.
precise: three steps (a load, an arithmetic operation, a store); when not atomic, another thread's store can fall between them.
source: D3 of F6-13 (Hwu, Kirk, El Hajj, "Programming Massively Parallel Processors: A Hands-on Approach") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a device-wide scan in three passes: tile sums, a scan of those, then each tile with its offset.
analogy: count per table, the head adds the counts, tables number their plates.
precise: needs about 3n memory accesses (read, read, write) plus the small middle pass; the kernel boundaries are the grid-wide barriers (F6-12).
source: D3 of F6-16 (Hwu, Kirk, El Hajj, "Programming Massively Parallel Processors: A Hands-on Approach") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: combining many values into one, such as a sum, maximum or count.
analogy: turning everyone's pile of coins into one total.
precise: applying an associative binary operator ⊕ to n values; a tree evaluation takes n − 1 operations in ⌈log₂ n⌉ steps; the result equals the sequential one exactly only when ⊕ is truly associative (integer addition), not for floating-point addition.
source: D3 of F6-14 (Hwu, Kirk, El Hajj, "Programming Massively Parallel Processors: A Hands-on Approach") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a block is resident when it has a place on an SM and can run.
analogy: a table that is inside the hall, not waiting outside.
precise: a block occupies an SM's registers, shared memory and thread slots from its start until it finishes; blocks beyond what all SMs can hold wait until resident blocks finish, and the programming model does not let you assume any order or co-residency between blocks.
source: D1 of F6-12 (NVIDIA, "CUDA C++ Programming Guide") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: for every position, the total of everything up to it.
analogy: each table's starting plate number.
precise: for input x and associative ⊕, output yi = x0 ⊕ … ⊕ xi (inclusive).
source: D3 of F6-16 (Hwu, Kirk, El Hajj, "Programming Massively Parallel Processors: A Hands-on Approach") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: writing each item to a computed position, not the next one.
analogy: each helper carries a plate to the shelf spot it was given.
precise: out[dst[i]] = in[i] with dst a permutation; on a GPU its store pattern decides how well writes coalesce (F6-08).
source: D3 of F6-18 (Wen-mei Hwu, David Kirk, Izzat El Hajj, "Programming Massively Parallel Processors: A Hands-on Approach") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a small, fast memory that the threads of one block share and fill themselves.
analogy: the table in the middle of a row group.
precise: on-chip memory allocated per thread block, declared with __shared__, visible to all threads of that block and only for the lifetime of the block; the kernel itself writes it, synchronises and reads it. Not the same as shared memory between processes (OS304).
source: D1 of F6-10 (NVIDIA, "CUDA C++ Programming Guide") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: input where a few values are far more common than the rest.
analogy: a delivery that is nine-tenths apples.
precise: in this chapter, a test input where 9 of every 10 bytes are 0 and the rest are spread over all 256 values (Listing 2's sample, kind 1).
source: R2 of F6-17 (run of Listing 2 (privatize_model.log), g++ 13.3.0, exit code 0.) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: one pass of radix sort with a one-bit digit: all keys with a 0 go first, then all with a 1, each group in its old order.
analogy: plates with an even number to the left, odd to the right, keeping the order.
precise: destination = exclusive scan of the 0-flags for 0-keys, and (number of 0-keys) + (number of 1-keys before me) for 1-keys.
source: D3 of F6-18 (Wen-mei Hwu, David Kirk, Izzat El Hajj, "Programming Massively Parallel Processors: A Hands-on Approach") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: equal keys keep their original order.
analogy: plates with the same middle digit stay in the order they arrived.
precise: if ki = kj and i < j in the input, the item from i comes first in the output; std::stable_sort guarantees it; the installed CUB header states "DeviceRadixSort is stable".
source: D4 of F6-18 (Thomas H. Cormen, Charles E. Leiserson, Ronald L. Rivest, Clifford Stein, "Introduction to Algorithms") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a shared array whose size is fixed when you compile, or one whose size you choose when you launch.
analogy: a table built to one size, or a folding table opened to the size you ask for.
precise: a __shared__ array with a compile-time size, or an extern __shared__ array whose size in bytes is the third parameter of the execution configuration <<<grid, block, bytes>>>.
source: D1 of F6-10 (NVIDIA, "CUDA C++ Programming Guide") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a calculation where every output uses a fixed pattern of nearby inputs.
analogy: every flatbread's topping uses the seven nearest bowls.
precise: out[i] = f(in[i−R], …, in[i+R]) for a fixed radius R; here f is a sum.
source: D3 of F6-10 (Wen-mei Hwu, David Kirk, Izzat El Hajj, "Programming Massively Parallel Processors: A Hands-on Approach") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: shuffling where each element of a row is stored, in a way you can undo, so that columns spread over the banks without wasting space.
analogy: each card's spices are put in its drawers in a different, fixed order.
precise: storing element (r, c) at column c XOR r (within a row of 32) instead of c; reading and writing use the same mapping.
source: D3 of F6-11 (Wen-mei Hwu, David Kirk, Izzat El Hajj, "Programming Massively Parallel Processors: A Hands-on Approach") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the piece of a big array that one block copies to its table and works on.
analogy: the stretch of bowls one group puts on its table.
precise: a contiguous sub-block of the data, sized by the programmer, that a thread block stages in shared memory to reuse it (MA201 uses "tile" for a sub-block of a matrix).
source: D3 of F6-10 (Wen-mei Hwu, David Kirk, Izzat El Hajj, "Programming Massively Parallel Processors: A Hands-on Approach") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a transpose that goes through a small square in shared memory so that both global reads and global writes are along rows.
analogy: a square of jars set on the table and picked up by columns.
precise: a block loads a TILE × TILE tile with row-wise (coalesced) reads, synchronises, and writes the tile's columns as rows of the output tile at the swapped block coordinates.
source: D2 of F6-19 (NVIDIA, "CUDA C++ Best Practices Guide") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: turning a matrix so that rows become columns.
analogy: moving jars so each shelf row becomes a column in the new pantry.
precise: for an input of h rows and w columns in row-major order, out[c * h + r] = in[r * w + c]; the output has w rows of h elements.
source: R2 of F6-19 (run of Listing 2 (transpose_audit.log), g++ 13.3.0, exit code 0.) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: add in pairs, then pairs of pairs.
analogy: rounds of pairing up in the row.
precise: step k combines elements 2k apart; in shared memory each step needs a barrier (F6-12).
source: D3 of F6-14 (Hwu, Kirk, El Hajj, "Programming Massively Parallel Processors: A Hands-on Approach") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the group of threads that the hardware runs together, 32 on NVIDIA, 32 or 64 on AMD.
analogy: a row of helpers.
precise: as defined in HW301 (F1-57); the width is warpSize, which in HIP 5.7 is a compile-time constant __AMDGCN_WAVEFRONT_SIZE.
source: H3 of F6-15 (HIP 5.7 headers as installed, read in this build: hip/amd_detail/amd_warp_functions.h (warpSize = __AMDGCN_WAVEFRONT_SIZE; __shfl, __shfl_up, __shfl_down, __shfl_xor lane rules on __builtin_amdgcn_ds_bpermute), amd_) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the lanes of a warp combine their updates, and one lane makes a single atomic for all.
analogy: the row counts its plates, one helper walks to the wall.
precise: use a warp vote (__ballot_sync, F6-15) and __popc to count passing lanes, elect a leader with __ffs, and issue one atomic with the total.
source: H1 of F6-13 (CUDA 12.0 headers as installed (nvidia-cuda-dev 12.0.146~12.0.1-4build4), read in this build: sm_60_atomic_functions.h (atomicAdd_block, atomicAdd_system), sm_30_intrinsics.h (__ballot_sync). Tier 1.) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a lane reads a register of another lane in its warp directly.
analogy: passing coins hand to hand along the row, no table needed.
precise: __shfl_down_sync(mask, v, delta) returns v of lane self + delta; no shared memory and no block barrier; see F6-15.
source: H1 of F6-14 (CUDA 12.0 headers as installed (nvidia-cuda-dev 12.0.146~12.0.1-4build4), read in this build: sm_30_intrinsics.h (__shfl_down_sync), crt/sm_80_rt.h (__reduce_add_sync). Tier 1.) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: every lane gives a yes or no; the result tells every lane who said yes.
analogy: raising hands.
precise: __ballot_sync(mask, p) returns a bit mask with bit k set when lane k is in mask and its predicate is true; __all_sync and __any_sync reduce it to one bit. The same term as in HW301.
source: H1 of F6-15 (CUDA 12.0 headers as installed (nvidia-cuda-dev 12.0.146~12.0.1-4build4), read in this build: sm_30_intrinsics.h (__shfl_*_sync, __ballot_sync, __activemask, __syncwarp), crt/sm_80_rt.h (__reduce_add_sync). Tier 1.) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: code that assumes the lanes of a warp move in lockstep.
analogy: assuming the whole row always moves in step, without anyone saying "now".
precise: an old practice (implicit synchronisation through shared memory inside a warp) that is unsafe since independent thread scheduling (compute capability 7.0); replace with _sync primitives or __syncwarp().
source: D1 of F6-15 (NVIDIA, "CUDA C++ Programming Guide") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)
